title: West Asia war, the Strait of Hormuz and India’s oil bill
dek: How the US–Iran conflict disrupted the world’s most important oil route, and why it matters so much to India.
seoTitle: Strait of Hormuz crisis 2026 timeline: oil prices and India
bigLabel: Up from about $65 a barrel before the crisis

glance.what: Since strikes on Iran in March 2026, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted and oil prices have swung between about $80 and over $100.
glance.why: India imports most of its crude oil, and a large share of its oil, LNG and almost all its LPG has passed through Hormuz.
glance.next: Any reopening of Hormuz shipping lanes, or a lasting ceasefire, would ease prices quickly.

forYou: Higher oil prices feed into petrol, diesel, cooking gas and airfares, and weaken the rupee.
next: Any reopening of Hormuz shipping lanes.

events.title: Strikes on Iran; the Strait of Hormuz closes
events.summary: After US and Israeli strikes on Iran, Hormuz shipping is shut. Brent ends the week near a seven-month high of about $73.

events.title: Tankers hit; shipping lines suspend Hormuz routes
events.summary: At least three tankers are damaged and Maersk suspends all cargo through the strait. Brent closed above $79 on 3 March, up from about $65 before the crisis.

events.title: Brent crosses $100
events.summary: Oil climbs back above $100 a barrel as the disruption drags on.

events.title: Blockade continues as peace talks stall
events.summary: Brent trades at $102.40 on 23 April and above $106 the next day.

events.title: Ceasefire news brings relief
events.summary: Brent falls about 4% to around $84 on news of a ceasefire and hopes that Hormuz shipping will normalise.

events.title: Oil back above $90
events.summary: A US–Iran deadlock keeps Hormuz disrupted, raising India’s import bill and pressure on the rupee.

events.title: Brent nears $100 again
events.summary: A fresh escalation in the US–Iran conflict renews fears for Gulf supplies, with Hormuz shipping still severely disrupted.
